title: Product Set Lower Bound for Small Sumsets
description: If |A+A| ≤ K|A| (small sumset), is |AA| ≥ |A|²/(log|A|)^C for some C? Answer: YES. Solymosi (2009) proved the stronger bound |AA| ≥ c(K)·|A|²/log|A|. This file reduces the problem to Solymosi's multiplicative-energy upper bound E×(A) ≤ C·|A+A|²·log|A| (the single axiom) and proves everything else, including the corrected (K-dependent) quantifiers.

overview.historicalContext: This problem is part of the sum-product phenomenon, a central topic in additive combinatorics. Erdős-Szemerédi conjectured that finite sets cannot have both small sumsets AND small product sets. This problem explores a conditional version: if the sumset is small, how large must the product set be? Solymosi's 2009 paper resolved this completely. The sum-product conjecture (1983) was proved in quantitative forms by Elekes (1997) using the Szemerédi-Trotter incidence theorem, and by Solymosi and others achieving exponent 4/3. The conditional question asks whether small additive structure forces large multiplicative structure, refining the unconditional sum-product estimates.
overview.problemStatement: Let A be a finite set of integers with |A+A| ≤ K·|A| for some constant K. Is it true that |A·A| ≥ |A|²/(log|A|)^C for some constant C > 0? (The implied constant in the conclusion necessarily depends on K.)
overview.text: This formalization captures Erdős Problem #818, a conditional form of the sum-product phenomenon. The Lean file defines sumsets, product sets, additive and multiplicative energy, and the small-sumset condition |A+A| ≤ K|A|. Its architecture isolates the single deep input — Solymosi's multiplicative-energy upper bound E×(A) ≤ C·|A+A|²·log|A|, which is a true theorem of additive combinatorics not yet in Mathlib — as the file's one axiom (solymosi_energy_bound). Everything else is proved from it. The Cauchy–Schwarz lower bound |A|⁴ ≤ |A·A|·E×(A) is proved axiom-free (cauchy_schwarz_energy) via Mathlib's Finset.le_card_mul_mul_mulEnergy. Combining the two energy bounds and squaring |A+A| ≤ K|A| yields the product-set estimate |A·A| ≥ |A|²/(C·K²·log|A|) (productSet_lower_bound_of_smallSumset), from which Solymosi's theorem, the Erdős conjecture (C=1), key_insight and proof_outline follow. A prior version of this file axiomatized the entire conclusion with the quantifier order ∃c,∀K; that statement is in fact FALSE — fixing c before K and taking K large makes the small-sumset hypothesis vacuous, forcing |AA| ≥ c|A|²/log|A| for every set, which geometric progressions (|AA|=2|A|−1) violate. The honest statement makes c depend on K (∀K,∃c), which is what is now proved. The earlier proof sketch also used the dimensionally-inconsistent energy bound E×≤|A|²·|A+A|·log and target |A|²/(K·log); the correct Solymosi bound is E×≤C·|A+A|²·log, giving the |A|²/(C·K²·log) estimate with K². The formalization has 7 definitions, 10 theorems, and 1 axiom, with 0 sorries; #print axioms confirms every headline theorem depends only on solymosi_energy_bound (plus the standard foundational axioms).
overview.proofStrategy: Sandwich the multiplicative energy: a Cauchy–Schwarz lower bound E×(A) ≥ |A|⁴/|A·A| (proved) and Solymosi's upper bound E×(A) ≤ C·|A+A|²·log|A| (axiom). With |A+A| ≤ K|A| this gives |A|⁴/|A·A| ≤ C·K²·|A|²·log|A|, i.e. |A·A| ≥ |A|²/(C·K²·log|A|). Setting c(K)=1/(C·K²) recovers Solymosi's |A·A| ≥ c·|A|²/log|A| and (with C=1) the Erdős conjecture.
keyInsights: Sets cannot have both strong additive AND multiplicative structure
Small additive doubling forces large multiplicative expansion
Multiplicative energy is the key intermediate quantity, sandwiched between two bounds
Solymosi's bound contributes K² (not K) because it controls energy by |A+A|²
The implied constant c necessarily depends on the doubling threshold K (∀K,∃c, not ∃c,∀K)
The log factor is tight (arithmetic progressions, via the Erdős multiplication-table problem)

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #818 asked whether small sumsets force large product sets. Solymosi (2009) proved YES: if |A+A| ≤ K|A|, then |A·A| ≥ c(K)·|A|²/log|A|. This file reduces the result to Solymosi's multiplicative-energy bound E×(A) ≤ C·|A+A|²·log|A| (its one axiom) and proves the product-set estimate |A·A| ≥ |A|²/(C·K²·log|A|), the Solymosi theorem, and the (corrected) Erdős conjecture from it — with 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications:
Solymosi's resolution of Erdős #818 demonstrates the energy method as a bridge between additive and multiplicative structure: sandwich the multiplicative energy E×(A) between a Cauchy–Schwarz lower bound |A|⁴/|A·A| and a sumset-dependent upper bound, then read off the product-set estimate.

The deep, irreducible input is Solymosi's bound E×(A) ≤ C·|A+A|²·log|A| (Advances in Mathematics, 2009), proved by a dyadic decomposition of slopes that Mathlib does not yet contain; this file isolates it as its single axiom (solymosi_energy_bound) rather than axiomatizing the conclusion. The Cauchy–Schwarz lower bound is proved axiom-free (cauchy_schwarz_energy) via Mathlib's Finset.le_card_mul_mul_mulEnergy, and the quantitative estimate |A·A| ≥ |A|²/(C·K²·log|A|) is then a machine-checked derivation (productSet_lower_bound_of_smallSumset) — the former proof_outline sorry is gone.

Two correctness issues in the earlier version were fixed. First, the quantifier order: the statement ∃c,∀K,∀A (|A+A|≤K|A| → |AA|≥c|A|²/log|A|) is false, because a fixed c cannot survive taking K large (which makes the hypothesis hold for all sets, including geometric progressions with |AA|=2|A|−1). The faithful statement ∀K,∃c(K) is now proved. Second, the energy bound and target were dimensionally inconsistent (E×≤|A|²·|A+A|·log and |A|²/(K·log)); Solymosi's genuine bound is E×≤C·|A+A|²·log, which yields the |A|²/(C·K²·log) estimate with the correct K² dependence.

The result connects to the broader Erdős–Szemerédi sum-product conjecture (Problem #52): once the sumset is constrained, the product set must compensate almost quadratically. The tightness of the logarithmic factor follows from the Erdős multiplication-table problem ({1,…,n} has |A+A|=2n−1 but |AA|≍n²/log n), so C=1 is best possible. The energy method formalized here underlies incidence-geometry, exponential-sum, and finite-field sum-product results across modern combinatorial number theory.
openQuestions: Can Solymosi's multiplicative-energy bound E×(A) ≤ C·|A+A|²·log|A| itself be formalized in Lean/Mathlib, removing the last axiom?
What is the optimal constant c(K) in |A·A| ≥ c(K)·|A|²/log|A|, and is the K² dependence sharp?
Do analogous energy bounds and sum-product estimates hold over other rings (e.g. finite fields, function fields)?

The logarithmic factor in Solymosi's bound reflects the same log-growth that appears in the harmonic series; the multiplication table problem's n²/log n estimate connects to prime counting
The energy method in Problem #818 is analogous to second-moment arguments: multiplicative energy counts pair collisions, paralleling variance-based probabilistic estimates
